lines: HC-1: drives a Haken Eagan Matrix instrument over MIDI — its preset list, its favourites, and knobs and CV for the macros, the recirculator and the output level
Sets that macro on the device; the panel shows the name the preset gives it, or a Roman numeral where the preset names none
Sets that recirculator parameter; the panel label changes with the recirculator the preset uses
Sets the recirculator mix
Sets the device's post level
Silences the device while it is on
Switches the knob beside it between absolute and relative control voltage: absolute makes a patched cable set the value on its own, relative adds the cable to the knob
Turns the recirculator on and off; this setting is global and does not change with the preset
Turns the recirculator's extended half-sample-rate computation on and off; the setting returns to the preset's own when you reload the preset
Sets that macro from a cable, 0V to 10V on its own or added to the knob when its relative button is on
Sets that recirculator parameter from a cable, 0V to 10V on its own or added to the knob when its relative button is on; this is the R1 jack, despite the maker's tooltip reading R2
Sets the recirculator mix from a cable, 0V to 10V on its own or added to the knob when its relative button is on
Sets the post level from a cable, 0V to 10V on its own or added to the knob when its relative button is on
Mutes the device on a trigger
A trigger once the device has finished initialising and is ready to play
Menu — Restore last preset at startup — selects the preset this module last had, instead of leaving the device on whatever preset it is showing
Menu — Use saved system presets — starts from the stored list of system presets instead of reading them back from the device
Menu — Use saved user presets — starts from the stored list of user presets instead of reading them back from the device
Menu — Refresh current preset — requests the settings of the preset the device is on
Menu — Refresh User presets — reads the list of user presets back from the device
Menu — Refresh System presets — reads the list of system presets back from the device
Menu — Center knobs — puts every knob at its middle position
Menu — Center Macro knobs — puts the six macro knobs at their middle position
Menu — Zero knobs — puts every knob except the volume at zero
Menu — Absolute CV — puts every control into absolute mode
Menu — Relative CV — puts every control into relative mode
Menu — Recirculator: Reverb, Mod delay, Swept Echo, Analog Echo, Delay LPF, Delay HPF — changes the recirculator the device is using until the preset is reloaded
Menu — Reboot HC-1 — starts the whole connection over and re-reads every user and system preset from the device
Menu — Send one handshake (ping) — pings the device once, which takes a fresh reading of its DSP usage
Menu — Remake QSPI data — rebuilds the device's additive data, as the Haken Editor does
Note — this module takes a minute or two the first time it runs, while it finds the device, opens the MIDI ports and reads every preset; the row of dots along the bottom is blue once it is ready
Note — CV inputs are read only once the device has reached that ready state
Note — the preset list, the tabs, the heart and the paging buttons are drawn by the module rather than built from knobs, so no click on them reaches this help
Note — switching the recirculator to Analog Echo with the feedback or the mix high can produce damagingly loud output
Note — the maker wrote this for Eagan Matrix firmware 10.09, and says some features do not work on later firmware

pachde-hc-1.notes: Input 6 is the R1 jack but is named R2 by the maker: configInput is called with "R2" for both R1_INPUT and R2_INPUT at HC-1.cpp lines 56 and 57, so the R1 jack wears its neighbour's tooltip. The panel prints R1, and the parameter for the same control is named R1.

lines: HC-2: a development module the maker uses for experiments, drawing running maps of the MIDI control codes travelling to and from the Eagan Matrix
Note — this module has no knobs, no jacks and no menu of its own; the two maps show the last value of each control code, the upper one for channel 1 and the lower one for channel 16
Note — the maps are cleared whenever a new preset starts loading, and hovering over one names the control code, what it is for and its current value
Note — the maker describes this module as hidden and meant for development rather than for playing
Favorites: sixteen buttons, each holding one HC-1 favourites file, so a set list can be loaded with one click
Note — this module does nothing on its own: it needs an HC-1 in the patch, which it finds by itself, so it can be placed anywhere in the rack rather than beside it
Note — the buttons come up empty: right-click one to choose a favourites file, or drag a file onto it, before it does anything
Note — clicking a button loads its file into the HC-1 Favorite tab and lights the button; clicking it again makes HC-1 forget the file, leaving the favourites themselves listed
Note — the sixteen buttons are drawn by the module rather than built as knobs, so no click on them reaches this help
Note — for more than sixteen files, add a second Favorites module
Note — save the module as a Rack preset once it is set up, and the same set of files can be brought into other patches
pachde-hc-favorites.notes: The module declares one parameter, Current, holding which button is selected. It has no widget of its own — the buttons are drawn by a custom widget — so it can never be clicked and is left untagged.

lines: Round: the Eagan Matrix rounding controls — how fast a note slides to its rounded pitch, which scale it rounds to, and when rounding applies
Sets how fast a note moves to its rounded pitch, 0 to 127, from no rounding through slow to very fast
Turns initial rounding on and off
Chooses when rounding applies, marked Normal, Release, Y and inverse Y; right-click it to pick from a menu
Picks the tuning scale that notes are rounded to, 12-tone equal temperament by default; right-click it to pick from a menu
Switches the rate knob between absolute and relative control voltage: absolute makes a patched cable set the rate on its own, relative adds the cable to the knob
Sets the rounding rate from a cable, 0V to 10V on its own or added to the knob when the relative button is on
Turns initial rounding on or off on a trigger
Note — this module does nothing on its own: it needs an HC-1 in the patch, which it finds by itself, so it can be placed anywhere in the rack rather than beside it
Note — the lights along the top show the rounding state the Continuum shows in the corner of its own display

lines: Pedal-1: the Eagan Matrix's pedal 1 — what the pedal controls, its range, and a virtual pedal that can be played from the panel or from a cable
Picks what the pedal controls, as one of the device's control codes; click to step forward, hold Ctrl and click to step back, or right-click for the whole list
Sets the pedal's value, 0 to 127; drag the handle, click anywhere on the bar, or roll the wheel over it
Sets the lowest value the pedal reaches, 0 to 127
Sets the highest value the pedal reaches, 0 to 127
Sets the pedal value from a cable, 0V to 10V across the pedal's range
The pedal's current value as 0V to 10V, whether it was moved by a real pedal or on the panel
Note — this module does nothing on its own: it needs an HC-1 in the patch, which it finds by itself, so it can be placed anywhere in the rack rather than beside it
Note — with the mouse over the value bar, Home and End jump to the top and bottom, Page Up and Page Down move by ten, the arrow keys move by one, and the number keys 1 to 0 step across the range
Note — the image under the value shows which pedal the device has detected, and hovering over it names that pedal; some pedals are only recognised once they have been moved
Note — the three buttons beside the value bar jump to the top, the middle and the bottom of the range, and are drawn by the module rather than built as knobs, so no click on them reaches this help
